title: The Fried Liver Attack
setupTitle: Five moves to the fork in the road

end.playFrom: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6

setup.label: Bishop to c4, aimed at f7
Knight to g5, the second attacker

beats.say: The Fried Liver is the most famous trap in the Italian Game. Your bishop and knight gang up on f7, and if Black takes back the wrong way, the black king gets dragged into the middle.
It's popular for a reason. Under 1800 in our Lichess sample, about a third of White players go knight to g5 here. After d5, Black takes back the wrong way almost half the time.
But Black has good answers too. We'll learn the attack, its mating patterns, then each refutation and what you do against it.
The script is our own, checked move by move with Stockfish. You're White.

beats.card: Five moves to the fork in the road
beats.say: Five moves. Watch the list tick itself off.
e4, e5, then your knight hits e5 and Black guards it.
Bishop to c4, aimed at f7. Only the black king guards that pawn.
Black's knight comes out and hits e4. That's the Two Knights Defence.
Knight to g5. Two pieces now hit f7, and only the king defends it. Black has to do something right now.
Three times in four, Black blocks the bishop with d5.
You take. Now Black chooses, and everything depends on how they take back. Stockfish calls it level, about plus 0.1.

chapters.title: The Fried Liver
chapters.from: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5

beats.say: The natural recapture is knight takes d5. It looks fine. It loses the right to castle.
Knight takes d5. Its bishop on c4 is now blocked, and f7 is guarded only by the king.
Knight takes f7! It forks the queen and the rook. Stockfish: about plus 0.9.
The king has to take, or Black just loses the rook.
Queen to f3, check. It also hits the d5 knight a second time.
Ke6 is Black's best. The king steps forward to guard d5 and walks into the middle.
Knight to c3. Now three pieces hit d5, and the knight there can't move: it's pinned to the king.
Black's best is knight to b4, guarding d5 and eyeing c2.
Castle. Your king is safe, theirs is in the middle.
c6 props up d5 one more time.
d4 opens lines to the king on e6. Stockfish: about plus 0.7. You're a piece down, with the better position.

beats.reset: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Nxd5 Nxf7 Kxf7 Qf3+ Ke6 Nc3 Ncb4
beats.say: Old books play a3, kicking the knight. It's a mistake.
The knight takes c2 with check and forks the rook. Stockfish now prefers Black. Queen to e4 is no better. Castle.

beats.reset: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Nxd5
beats.say: One more option: d4 at once, the Lolli Attack. Stockfish rates it about plus 0.7, close to the Fried Liver. Pick one and know it.

chapters.title: Mating patterns
chapters.from: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Nxd5 Nxf7 Kxf7 Qf3+

beats.say: Under 1800, Black finds king to e6 only about a third of the time. Here's how to punish the others.
King to g8, about one in ten. It hides behind its pawns, and walks into mate.
Bishop takes d5, check.
If the queen takes, you take back with check.
The bishop blocks, and queen takes e6 is mate. The king's own pawns box it in.

beats.reset: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Nxd5 Nxf7 Kxf7 Qf3+
beats.say: King back to e8, about one in three. Safer, but it gives back the piece.
Bishop takes d5, and queen to f7 is mate next move.
Black has to guard f7 with the queen.
Take the knight with check. You're a pawn up, Black's pawns are broken and the king can't castle. Stockfish: about plus 3.4.

beats.reset: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Nxd5 Nxf7 Kxf7 Qf3+
beats.say: Blocking with the queen, about one in four, drops the knight on d5.
Bishop takes d5, check. The bishop blocks.
Take the knight, then the pawn, and the queen hits the rook in the corner. Two pawns up, about plus 3.4.

beats.reset: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Nxd5 Nxf7 Kxf7 Qf3+
beats.say: King to e7 leaves d5 with one defender.
Bishop takes d5, back to even material.
The knight jumps at your queen.
Queen to f7, check, and the king has to walk up to d6. Stockfish: about plus three, and the king has no shelter.

beats.reset: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Nxd5 Nxf7 Kxf7 Qf3+ Ke6 Nc3 Ncb4 O-O c6 d4
beats.say: Back in the main line. If Black grabs the d4 pawn...
...the rook joins with check down the open file. Stockfish: about plus four, and more the deeper it looks. The king is out in the open with nowhere to hide.

chapters.title: Refutation one: Na5
chapters.from: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5

beats.card: The main line: knight to a5
beats.say: The best players don't take on d5. About a third of the time under 1800, Black plays knight to a5.
Knight to a5 hits your bishop. Black gives up a pawn for quick development.
Bishop to b5, check. Keep the bishop alive.
Black blocks, you take, Black takes back.
Bishop to e2. You're a pawn up, but your pieces are tangled.
h6 kicks your knight.
It goes back to f3, and e4 kicks it again.
Knight to e5, the best square. Stockfish calls it dead level.
So this is the honest truth: against knight to a5, the Fried Liver is over. You keep a pawn, Black keeps the activity. Play solid moves and castle.

chapters.title: Refutation two: b5 and Nd4
chapters.from: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5

beats.say: Two rarer tries hit your bishop with a pawn or a knight. One move handles both.
Pawn to b5 attacks the bishop.
Taking it looks greedy and good.
But the queen takes d5 and hits your bishop on b5 and the pawn on g2. Black is fine.

beats.reset: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 b5
beats.say: Instead, bishop all the way back to f1. It looks silly, but d5 stays defended and b5 is weak. About plus 0.5.

beats.reset: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5
beats.say: Knight to d4, about one in eight, threatens a fork on c2.
Kick it with c3.
Black chases the bishop, and it goes back to f1 again.
Black takes on d5, you take the knight, the queen takes yours.
Bishop takes b5 with check. The black king loses castling.
Castle. You're a pawn up, about plus 0.6.

chapters.title: Refutation three: the Traxler
chapters.from: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5

beats.say: The wildest answer ignores f7 completely. About one in eight under 1800.
Bishop to c5. Black lets you take f7 and goes after your f2.
Take with the bishop, with check. Stockfish: about plus 1.2, your best result against a sound defence.
The king moves.
Bishop back to b3. You're a pawn up and Black's king can't castle. Keep it simple from here.

beats.reset: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5
beats.say: Two in three players take with the knight instead, forking queen and rook.
Black ignores it: bishop takes f2, check. Now one slip and you're mated.
King to e2?
Knight to d4, check, and the black pieces swarm. Stockfish says Black is winning.

beats.reset: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Nxf7 Bxf2+
beats.say: Even the best line, king takes f2, is a fight. The knight comes in with check.
King to g1, queen to h4. The engine says it's level, if you find a string of only-moves.
Greed: knight takes the rook?
Queen to f2 is mate, guarded by the knight on e4. That's why you take on f7 with the bishop.

chapters.title: Your game plan
chapters.from: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5

beats.say: The whole thing in four lines.
One. If Black takes on d5 with the knight, take f7, check on f3, bring the knight to c3, castle, then d4.
Two. Against knight to a5, check on b5, drop the bishop to e2 and accept a level game, a pawn up.
Three. Against b5 or knight to d4, the bishop goes all the way back to f1.
Four. Against bishop to c5, take f7 with the bishop, not the knight.
So play it against Stockfish next. It won't fall for the trap, so you'll practise the refutations.
